title: Rhine and alpine rivers
deck: What the pipeline does with daily discharge at eight stations, before anything is mapped to XR.
steps: Daily discharge at eight stations, drawn as in Issue 6: one column per year, each station a layer stacked on a shared spine. Height is the year's mean flow relative to the station's own average year.
Each year is summarised by six scale-free numbers, so a glacial stream and a lowland river can be compared. Pick one to see it across the record.
One unsupervised model per station learns what a typical year looks like there. The score is how badly each year fits it. Colour runs from typical to most unusual, scaled within the station.
method: PCA with 2 components, one model per station, fitted on that station's complete years.
source: Four Rhine stations (GRDC): Lustenau, Basel, Köln, Lobith. Four alpine stations (FOEN): Weisse Lütschine–Zweilütschinen, Reuss–Andermatt, Aare–Brienzwiler, Aare–Thun.

features.label: Mean flow vs recent norm
features.desc: The year's mean flow against the mean of the 30 years before it (0 = normal).

features.label: Peak ratio
features.desc: log10 of the highest day divided by the year's mean flow: how sharp the biggest flood was.

features.label: Low-flow ratio
features.desc: The lowest day divided by the year's mean flow: how close the river came to running dry.

features.label: Flow-duration slope
features.desc: Steepness of the flow-duration curve: flashy rivers are steep, steady ones are flat.

features.label: Recession constant
features.desc: How slowly flow falls back after a peak: the river's memory of what it just carried.

features.label: Seasonal swing
features.desc: Highest monthly mean minus lowest, as a share of the year's mean.

limits: One model per station, fitted on that station's own years, so a score compares a year with its own station only. Colour is scaled within each station.

It flags unusual combinations of features, not extremes, and does not reliably flag droughts: the 1976 drought ranks 3rd of 70 years at Lustenau but 187th of 208 at Köln; the 1995 Köln flood ranks 101st.
The four alpine stations end in 2014; the Rhine stations end in 2020 (Lustenau, Basel, Lobith) and 2024 (Köln). Köln's first year (1816) has 61 days and is scored, not fitted.
Nothing here has been tested with viewers. A high score means the year was unusual for its station, not that a person would feel it so.
